units.translation: In ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧, to stitch together) we have the metaphor common since Homer (⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧). The comparison with the hare, according to the scholiast, points to the complete lack of resistance; or “like dogs tearing a hare to pieces.” The verse may be deliberately without caesura, because of ⟦7⟧, as in ⟦8⟧ and elsewhere; something like ⟦9⟧. 493. 883 is excluded here. 20. 27 f. After the transposition there is no longer any reason for the change ⟦10⟧ 20 (Blaydes). The river-god Pleistos, Poseidon, and Zeus now appear, after this transposition, as being named only in an appendix to the prayer; but this is also appropriate. The Pleistos flowed, according to ⟦11⟧, about 3 stades from Delphi and emptied into the sea at Kirrha; ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧. The local pronunciation was ⟦14⟧; nevertheless Herodian, E. M. 676, 5 (⟦15⟧.), made it barytone. Poseidon was the former possessor of Delphi, which he had exchanged for Kalaureia, Callimachus in the scholia, ⟦16⟧. ⟦17⟧, Aristonoos in the paean, see on 22 f. at the end; therefore (⟦18⟧) there was an altar of Poseidon in the sanctuary of Apollo.
⟦1⟧ periphrastic as in ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧; on this and on ⟦6⟧ cf. especially ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧⟦10⟧). Zeus in third and last place as in ⟦11⟧ (Weil).
of fulfillers the most fulfilling power, blessed Zeus
⟦1⟧ describes what the Pythia habitually does (on 21); in the contrast ⟦2⟧ . . ⟦3⟧ this emerges quite clearly.
⟦1⟧ 29 picks up the participle ⟦2⟧ again (⟦3⟧); cf. on 1.
The ⟦1⟧ is the same as in 18, in that the Pythia represents the god; thus the tripod, ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧.
and a woman sits on the holy tripod, etc.

The transmitted construction: ⟦1⟧, is at least not clear, since the object ⟦2⟧ has the appearance of an adverb; also ⟦3⟧ with accusative is not sufficiently secured for Aeschylus either by the corrupt verse ⟦4⟧ or by ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧ (“will prepare,” = ⟦7⟧). On the other hand, with ⟦8⟧ instead of ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧ becomes an unambiguous subject, and cf. ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧ (Turn. for ⟦14⟧) ⟦15⟧. ⟦16⟧ like ⟦17⟧ Thuc. 1, 1, 1 etc.; but what motivates the wish? On this day of oracle-giving there is nothing special that would cause one to expect or wish for special good fortune. So this too may be a formula, in which the wish is intensified as much as possible: each time she enters the temple, she prays thus.
may they grant me to obtain the best things than before
